spec.name: TRI_warranty_review_workflow
spec.description:
Initiate the warranty claim document processing workflow for a product not
purchased through the Focus Corp online shop (reseller or external purchase —
no internal order record exists). Call when the specialist's prompt indicates
the product was bought from a reseller, an external shop, or any source other
than Focus Corp, and the customer wants to file a warranty claim.
Required inputs: customer_id [Required], customer_name [Required],
customer_tier [Required], customer_email [Required], customer_phone [Required].
Do NOT call if under_warranty is already present in context for the product —
that means a Focus Corp order record exists; use the knowledge base options
lookup instead.
Returns: nothing — the workflow owns all document collection, extraction, HITL
review, and outcome steps, and presents the warranty outcome directly to the
specialist via its own closing step.

customer_id.description: Customer ID in format C-*, e.g. C-3DBZFE

customer_name.description: Full name of the customer, e.g. Marie Smith

customer_tier.description: Customer loyalty tier (Platinum, Gold, Silver, Bronze, Standard)

spec.name: tool_7c16d0
spec.description:
Check whether a catalog item purchased on a given date is still within its warranty period. Use when a catalog item ID and a purchase date are both known and the agent needs to determine warranty status and days remaining. Do NOT call if the warranty status is already known from the order item's under_warranty field — use that value directly. Returns: warranty_period, warranty_end_date, days_remaining (0 if expired), days_expired (0 if still in warranty).


**Responses:**

- **200** (Success): OK
  - Content-Type: `application/json`

  - **Response Properties:**

  - **Example:**
```json
{
  "warranty_status": "unknown_type"
}
```

purchase_date.description: [Required] Date the product was purchased in format YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2024-03-15.

catalog_item_id.description: [Required] Catalog item ID in format CI-*, e.g. CI-D412F3.

days_expired.description: the number of calendar days since warranty_end_date; 0 if the warranty is still active

error_message.description: Error message in case determining the warranty_status failed

days_remaining.description: the number of calendar days from today until warranty_end_date; 0 if the warranty has already expired

catalog_item_id.description: Catalog item ID in format CI-*, e.g. CI-D412F3

warranty_end_date.description: the date on which the warranty expires, calculated as purchase_date + warranty_duration

error_handler_config.error_message: Something went wrong while running 'Check Warranty Status'

spec.name: tool_d95294
spec.description:
Search the product catalog by free-text product name. Use when a product name is available (e.g. extracted from a receipt or warranty card) and the catalog item ID or category is unknown. Do NOT call if a catalog_item_id is already known — use get_catalog_item_by_id for a direct lookup. Returns: matchingItems[] — sorted by confidence descending; each with catalog_item_id, name, description, category, sub_category, price.


**Responses:**

- **200** (Success): OK
  - Content-Type: `application/json`

  - **Response Properties:**

    - **matchingItems**: { matchingItems: catalog_item[] } — sorted by confidence descending; best match is first. A confidence value of 100 means a complete match on the item name.

  - **Example:**
```json
{
  "matchingItems": [
    "unknown_type"
  ]
}
```

product_name.description: [Required] Free-text product name to search for, e.g. "Lenovo Gamer Z2". Partial and case-insensitive matches are accepted.

matchingItems.description: { matchingItems: catalog_item[] } — sorted by confidence descending; best match is first. A confidence value of 100 means a complete match on the item name.

error_handler_config.error_message: Something went wrong while running 'Lookup Catalog Item'

spec.fn:
ws = flow["Handle Warranty Claim"]["Select customer product"].output
selected_option = (ws.get("Customer product", "") if isinstance(ws, dict) else getattr(ws, "Customer product", "")) or ""

marker = "Catalog Item Id: "
if marker in selected_option:
    # Split on the marker and strip the trailing closing parenthesis
    flow.private.catalog_item_id = selected_option.split(marker)[-1].rstrip(")").strip()
else:
    flow.private.catalog_item_id = None
spec.name: script_1b53ac
script_376040
spec.display_name: Extract Warranty Fields (flatten for decision table)

spec.fn:
# Retrieve the list of matching items from the previous step
items = flow["Handle Warranty Claim"]["Lookup Catalog Item"].output.matchingItems or []

# Initialize defaults
flow.private.catalog_item_id = None
self.output.options = []

# Check if the first item has a confidence of 100
if items and items[0].get("confidence") == 100:
    flow.private.catalog_item_id = items[0].get("catalog_item_id")
else:
    # Filter items with confidence > 50 and format display strings
    self.output.options = [
        f"{item.get('name')} (Confidence: {item.get('confidence')}, Catalog Item Id: {item.get('catalog_item_id')})"
        for item in items
        if item.get("confidence", 0) > 50
    ]

output_schema.description:
The text extraction operation response when output_format is set to "object".

This class represents the structured response from a document text extraction operation,
containing both the extracted plain text and the complete document structure metadata
inherited from AssemblyJsonOutput.

Attributes:
    text (str): The extracted plain text content from the document. This is the 
               concatenated text from all pages and structures in reading order.
               Empty string if no text could be extracted.

Note:
    - This response type is used when DocProcSpec.output_format is set to 
      DocProcOutputFormat.object
    - For file reference responses, use TextExtractionResponse instead
    - The text field contains only plain text; structured data is in inherited fields
